talk_track: This is Daniel Kirichanski — I ran platform engineering at PayPal (the CI/CD platform serving 9,000+ developers) and at Ripple, where the job was exactly the layer Netic's postings describe. Your Founding Web Platform Engineer listing says the Next.js app 'is already in production and serving customers — what it needs now is real platform structure underneath it.' Posting that alongside a Founding Product Infrastructure Engineer is a specific confession: product teams outran the platform, and whatever conventions they improvise while those seats stay open become the platform. The first ninety days of a platform org are mostly decisions, not code — golden paths, paved-road delivery, and what the agent backbone refuses to support — and those can be settled before the hires land so your founding engineers inherit a direction instead of a cleanup. Which decision feels more urgent — web platform conventions or the agent backbone?
